parole.testo: From German Achse (“axis, axle”), from Middle High German ahse, from Old High German ahsa (“axis, axle”), from Proto-West Germanic *ahsu (“axle”), from Proto-Germanic *ahsō (“axle”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱs- (“axis, axle”), from *h₂eǵ- (“to drive”).

parole.significato: a partner dance in moderate duple time, traditionally classed as a type of gammeldans (“traditional Nordic round dance”)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Rheinländer (“Rhinelander; reinlender dance”), originally “a person from the Rhineland”, from Rheinland (“Rhineland”) and the inhabitant-forming suffix -er, with umlaut.
